events.title: Thirteenth Amendment Declared Ratified
events.description: U.S. Secretary of State William Seward announced that the Thirteenth Amendment to the U.S. Constitution had been ratified by three-fourths of the states, formally abolishing slavery and involuntary servitude except as punishment for a crime.
events.significance: Legally ended chattel slavery in the United States and marked a foundational step in the expansion of civil rights during Reconstruction.

events.title: Piltdown Man Announced
events.description: Charles Dawson and Arthur Smith Woodward announced the discovery of fossil fragments in Piltdown, England, claimed to be the 'missing link' between apes and humans.
events.significance: The find was exposed as a hoax in 1953, becoming one of the most famous scientific frauds and a lasting lesson about peer review and scientific skepticism.

events.title: Japan Admitted to the United Nations
events.description: Japan was admitted as a member of the United Nations, roughly eleven years after the end of World War II, following the normalization of relations with the Soviet Union that removed a Soviet veto.
events.significance: Marked Japan's return to the international community as a full participant in world affairs after postwar occupation and isolation.

events.title: The Nutcracker Premieres in St. Petersburg
events.description: Tchaikovsky's ballet The Nutcracker premiered at the Mariinsky Theatre in St. Petersburg, Russia, in a double bill with his opera Iolanta.
events.significance: Initially received with mixed reviews, it became one of the most popular and frequently performed ballets in the world, a staple of holiday traditions.

events.title: Birth of Steven Spielberg
events.description: Steven Spielberg, American filmmaker, was born in Cincinnati, Ohio. He went on to direct Jaws, E.T., Schindler's List, and Saving Private Ryan.
events.significance: Spielberg helped define the modern blockbuster and became one of the most influential and commercially successful directors in film history, winning multiple Academy Awards.
